chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abdullah ibn Jundub, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When it is the habit of a man to perform Hajj every year, then he stays behind for one year and does not go out, the angels who are on the earth say to those who are on the mountains: 'We have missed the voice of so-and-so.' So they say: 'Seek him.' So they seek him but do not find him, so they say: 'O Allah, if a debt withheld him, then pay it off for him, or if it was an illness, then cure him, or if it was poverty, then enrich him, or if it was imprisonment, then relieve him from it, or if it was a deed, then deal with it accordingly.' And the people are supplicating for themselves, while they are supplicating for the one who stayed behind.

key_terms.لِمَنْ تَخَلَّفَ: for the one who stayed behind

ai.seo_question: What do angels pray for when a regular pilgrim misses Hajj?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the enduring spiritual bond of the 'habitual pilgrim' (al-hajj al-mu'tad), whose consistent devotion earns him continuous angelic intercession even during absence. The narrative illustrates a unique cosmological dynamic where angels, acting as divine witnesses, actively seek out the missing believer and supplicate for his specific worldly and spiritual needs, contrasting with the general self-interest of humanity. This highlights the concept of *istiqra'* (consistency) in worship, suggesting that habitual piety creates a lasting merit that transcends temporary lapses.
